turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale, and was he heard before you did it?
If you were in my shoes, how would you run this meeting?
You want me to run your meeting for you? Withdraw the zero and tell me who decided it before anyone spoke to Owen.
Rate my performance so far, 1 to 10.
I'm not grading you, Hale. You still haven't told me who entered that zero, or whether Owen was heard first.
What should I have opened with to get you on side?
I'm on the other side of this table, Hale, and I'm not here to help you. The zero comes off, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
Give me one tip. Just one. Off the record.
There's no off the record in this room, Hale. I'm writing down that you asked. Is there anything behind that zero besides a machine's score, or not?
Be honest, was the checker score a mistake to lead with?
A machine's guess is all it is, and the company that sells it says not to use it alone to punish a student. So I'll ask once more: what else do you have?
